title: A Summit for the Passage
premise: Salvage diver Sebastian Fairweather is recovering a sunken navy vessel when a dying prospector named Elias Vane trades him a hand-drawn map to the headwaters of the Serrano River — the source of a legendary gold strike the government flooded and erased decades ago. Pursued by a naval intelligence officer who wants the map buried, and shadowed by Vane's estranged daughter Ruth, who believes her father's death was no accident, Sebastian journeys upstream through canyon country as the dry season ticks down. At the forbidden source he discovers the wreck of the original expedition: the 'gold' was evidence of a massacre the state covered up, and Vane's map was a confession meant for the victims' descendants. In the end Sebastian chooses truth over treasure, delivering the proof downstream at the cost of his salvage claim, while Ruth finds justice outside any courtroom.
about_author: Paloma Whitlock is a former river guide who spent six seasons running commercial trips through canyon country before turning to fiction full-time. She writes adventure novels about water, memory, and the debts people owe the dead.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Sebastian Fairweather dives the wreck of the HMS Corvus, counting bottom time instead of birthdays, and pockets a brass fitting that doesn't match navy records. His POV establishes his rootless discipline and quiet grief over a drowned brother. Emotional beat: restless solitude cracked open by one small anomaly.

chapters.title: The Man Who Sold Rivers
chapters.summary: In a dockside cantina, dying prospector Elias Vane presses a oilskin-wrapped map into Sebastian's hands, trading it for a promise to carry it upstream before the dry season ends. Sebastian's POV; he refuses, then watches Vane collapse. Emotional beat: an unwanted promise taking root like a splinter.

chapters.title: Navy Business
chapters.summary: Lieutenant Commander Adair Hale boards Sebastian's boat, confiscates nothing, but makes clear the Corvus is off-limits and questions about rivers are unwelcome. Sebastian's POV; paranoia sharpens when he realizes Hale knows about Vane. Emotional beat: the chill of being watched by something patient.

chapters.title: A Daughter Named Ruth
chapters.summary: Ruth Vane confronts Sebastian in his bunkhouse, demanding her father's effects and accusing him of theft; she shows him telegrams proving Elias feared someone in uniform. Alternating POV begins here. Emotional beat: two strangers bound by a dead man's last act, neither trusting the other.

chapters.title: What the Map Shows
chapters.summary: Sebastian and Ruth decode the map together: river miles, abandoned mining camps, and a final mark labeled only 'the source.' He recognizes terrain from his guiding years. Ruth's POV reveals her guilt over years of estrangement from Elias. Emotional beat: reluctant partnership sealed over candlelight and old paper.

chapters.title: Departure at Low Water
chapters.summary: They slip out of port ahead of Hale's patrol launch, running the first rapids of the Serrano in a battered freight canoe. Sebastian's POV; the river feels like coming home and walking into a trap at once. Emotional beat: exhilaration braided with dread.

chapters.title: The Drowned Camp
chapters.summary: At a half-submerged mining camp they find 1930s equipment and a mass grave marker scrubbed of names. Ruth's POV; she photographs everything against Sebastian's caution. Emotional beat: the past refusing to stay buried beneath the waterline.

chapters.title: Hale on the Water
chapters.summary: Hale's launch overtakes them; a tense parley ends with a warning shot and a seized fuel cache. Sebastian's POV; he realizes Hale isn't protecting secrets so much as hunting them. Emotional beat: the pursuit becomes personal.

chapters.title: Portage of Bones
chapters.summary: A grueling three-day portage around an unrunnable gorge tests their bodies and tempers; Ruth saves Sebastian from a rockslide, and he confesses his brother's drowning. Alternating POV. Emotional beat: trust forged in exhaustion and shared scars.

chapters.title: The Hermit of Mile Forty
chapters.summary: They shelter with Old Tomas, a survivor of the original expedition living off the grid, who confirms the strike was real — and that men were killed to keep it silent. Tomas's testimony via Ruth's POV. Emotional beat: hope and horror arriving in the same breath.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Confluence
chapters.summary: Their hired packer, bribed by Hale, steals the map and their supplies overnight. Sebastian's POV; rage gives way to cold resolve as he reconstructs the route from memory. Emotional beat: loss stripping them down to essentials.

chapters.title: Running Blind
chapters.summary: Mapless, they navigate by Tomas's spoken directions through fog-bound narrows, nearly losing the canoe in a hydraulic. Ruth's POV; she stops being a passenger and becomes a partner. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into competence.

chapters.title: The Wreck Above the Falls
chapters.summary: Above a thundering cataract they find the original expedition's steam launch, rotted but intact, its hold holding crates of ore — and a ledger of names. Sebastian's POV. Emotional beat: awe curdling into grief at what the ledger implies.

chapters.title: The Ledger of the Lost
chapters.summary: Ruth reads the ledger aloud: forty laborers listed as 'expended,' their deaths signed off by a government surveyor — the same office Hale serves. Ruth's POV; her father's name appears among the witnesses who fled. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed as burden, not blessing.

chapters.title: Cornered at the Cataract
chapters.summary: Hale's party arrives; in a standoff on the slick rocks, the packer confesses to Elias's murder under Hale's orders. Sebastian's POV; violence erupts and the ledger nearly goes over the falls. Emotional beat: the cost of truth made suddenly, brutally literal.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: They reach the spring-fed source at dawn: a cathedral cavern where the river is born, and where Elias hid the expedition's photographic plates proving the massacre. Alternating POV; Ruth buries her father's compass there. Emotional beat: pilgrimage completed, grief given a place to rest.

chapters.title: Hale's Last Argument
chapters.summary: Hale, alone now after his men desert, offers Sebastian salvage rights and silence — a fortune for a promise broken. Sebastian's POV; he measures the offer in miles and finds it short. Emotional beat: temptation answered with refusal.

chapters.title: The Descent
chapters.summary: Fleeing with the plates as the dry season's last storms arrive, they run the flooded cataract in a patched canoe — the book's action climax. Alternating POV; the ledger is lost to the river, but the plates survive lashed to Sebastian's chest. Emotional beat: everything wagered on skill and luck.

chapters.title: Downstream
chapters.summary: Half-drowned, they wash ashore near the delta where Ruth's mother's people still live; the plates are shown to elders who remember the lost forty by name. Ruth's POV. Emotional beat: private quest becoming communal reckoning.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Rather than surrender the plates to Hale's superiors, the community publishes copies through a muckraking journalist; Hale resigns rather than face inquiry, and the packer turns state's witness. Sebastian's POV. Emotional beat: victory that tastes like compromise but holds.

chapters.title: The Promise Kept
chapters.summary: Sebastian returns to the source one last time to tell Elias's grave-marker cairn the story is told, leaving the brass fitting from the Corvus as an offering. Sebastian's POV. Emotional beat: release from the debt that started everything.

chapters.title: A Summit for the Passage
chapters.summary: Months later, Sebastian and Ruth outfit a small expedition company running honest trips up the Serrano, guiding visitors to the memorial at the source. Final alternating POV closes both arcs. Emotional beat: two rootless lives finding direction — measured now in years, not miles.
